page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v4 is an ESv4-family virtual machine configured with 64 vCPUs and 504.0 GB of RAM, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor operating at 2.8 GHz, featuring 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, and cryptographic acceleration flags like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on external Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the E64s_v4 demonstrates strong memory performance, particularly in large-block uncached operations, achieving a read bandwidth of 300.14 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 134.52 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25 percent of tested servers. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 is also highly efficient at 255.76 GB/sec. However, single-threaded performance is more moderate, with bzip3 single-threaded decompression falling into the bottom 25 percent at 8.51 GB/sec. Large-scale integer and vector processing are supported by a strong PassMark CPU extended instructions score of 57,939.17. For web workloads, the instance delivers a high static web serving throughput of 48.4 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the E64s_v4 lies in its sequential text generation capabilities for language models; LLM text generation speeds are weak, dropping to 41.17 tokens/sec for small models and 7.11 tokens/sec for medium models, though prompt processing speeds remain average. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 7.88 GB per core and strong multi-threaded capabilities, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads such as large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise applications, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks.
